digest.component_or_area: LLM provider abstraction and parity testing harness
propositions: Bedrock must meet a non-inferiority parity bar before becoming a first-class LLM provider, with equivalence measured on structured-output validity, per-criterion verdict agreement, recall and false-accept rates, runtime error rate, and gold-coverage floor.

The parity harness must prove that identical payloads reach both providers, identical tool sets are available, provider routing is clean (no cross-provider calls), and any capability differences are explicit and symmetric.

Both Bedrock inference-profile IDs (sonnet-4-6 and opus-4-8) are invokable in account 896586841071/us-east-1; opus-4-8 rejects temperature=0 and is handled by the existing supports_temperature: False override.

The paired corpus run across 30 gold-labeled cases (15 block/15 advisory) at N=3 epochs per arm established that Bedrock clears payload and tool parity for both class slots, with provider-clean routing (zero non-Bedrock calls on v2 arms).

Residual decision-level flips (1 on standard, 2 on frontier) and frontier verdict agreement 0.929 are informational rather than gating criteria, as comparing two different models' judgements is out of scope per operator ruling.

The latency measurement shows Bedrock standard slot 9.9% faster than direct Anthropic and frontier within 0.1%, and a real expressiveness gap exists in Bedrock's cachePoint lacking a non-default TTL where Anthropic's cache_control carries one.
